assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.3 [19211,20299) contains the whole section. Its final sentence supplies designation, public acceptance, permanence and the version-specific choice. The preceding sentences independently establish the two other version-election routes.

challenge.method: Tested a designated proxy’s private assent, a public endorsement by an undesignated party, and a designated proxy’s public acceptance of one version. Separately tested an express numbered-or-later grant and a grant without a version number.
challenge.results: Private assent and an undesignated party’s announcement each lack a required element. A designated proxy’s public acceptance gives a lasting choice of the accepted version. It neither forces migration nor approves every future version. A separately authorized numbered-or-later grant permits the specified version or a later FSF-published non-draft version without proxy acceptance. Where the Document specifies no number, §10 separately permits any FSF-published non-draft version.

limitations: The publisher plaintext supplies the rule. Applying it to a work requires its authorized terms and evidence of the proxy’s actual public acceptance of the particular version. An illustrative addendum or catalog identifier establishes neither fact.
reasoning: GNU 1.3 §10 makes the proxy’s authority depend on the Document designating that proxy to decide which future versions may be used. The designated proxy’s public statement accepting a particular version permanently gives licensees the option to choose it for that Document.
